text:
Mark Stone is 34, the Golden Knights' captain, and two points from Vegas' career scoring record after the Utah win, per TSN. He has 11 goals and 21 points in 22 games, with 11 of those points on the power play.

The goals come with a warning label. He has 11 on 8.1 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and he's shooting 27% after 22% last season. The chances are real; that finishing rate rarely lasts. Vegas has also scored 9.9 more goals than expected with him on the ice, and his last ten games show it starting to even out: 6 points against the 10.4 our numbers expected.

The rest of his game is why he matters. Evolving-Hockey had him 3rd of 401 forwards last season at 4.1 wins above replacement, with opponents getting fewer chances when he played (94th percentile). After a 6-3 loss to Vancouver he told The Athletic's Jesse Granger, "I don't think we managed momentum very well." The record will come; how he and Vegas tidy up five-on-five is the bigger thing to watch.
headline: Stone's finishing is running hot
